main_text.p: πνέλῳ, labrum balneatorium: vas quodvis majus, sed ligneum, proprie; a boale Idem πνέλῳ vel πνελὶς, σφυ-δόνη: pala annuli. Anglis, (ita repe-rio:) nescio unde, nisi hinc, a beztll.

Πυσαείζιν, Hesych. exponit, μὴ ἀνέ-χεσθαί τῆν, ἀλλ' ἀπωσπάζειν: χαλεπαίνειν: id est, ex impatientia & indignatione refilire, molestè ferre. Angli de tumul-tuante dicunt, to keep a pudder. Affi-nis vox χολυδυνλίζω, quam Hesychius exponit, θυμῶδες: irasci, indignari, to grunt.
Πεδάζω, vel πεδάω, impedire, ligare; to bînde: πέδη, pedica, vinculum, a bond.
Πλάσσω, formo; creo, compono, fingo, effingo; to plott.

Παίω, Graecus Aristophanis Scholia-stes: τὸ παίζειν λέγεται, τὸ παῖν ἐπῶν συμβόλων παίειν, id est, τὸ παίζειν, proprie, quidvis expedite facere. Angli similiter, to plg. Suspicetur aliquis fortasse ex Latino, applicare. Sed longè alia syntaxis: Dicunt enim Latini, „applicare animum ad aliquid: Angli, to applp the mind.

page.notes: Greek passages are only approximately legible at this scan resolution; Greek and English glosses in the old black-letter-influenced type are rendered as best read. Several English words (e.g. "beztll", "bînde", "plg.") are doubtful and should be checked against the original.
